RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 exit) — root cause CONFIRMED at runtime.

MECHANISM. `RunawayPaginationError` is declared `class RunawayPaginationError(RuntimeError)`
at adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:29. Its MRO, printed from a live import, is:

  (RunawayPaginationError, RuntimeError, Exception, BaseException, object)
  issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError) == False

`fetch_snapshot`'s three enrichment blocks each match on the CORE type
(fetcher.py:621 parent, :668 comment, :708 issuelink — `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise`).
Cloud's error is not in that type's hierarchy, so all three re-raise clauses MISS it and control
falls through to the next clause, the broad `except Exception` fail-open (fetcher.py:625/672/712),
which logs a warning and degrades.

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT (runtime, not static). Drove the real `fetch_snapshot` (loaded from
source, `_load_acli` patched) with a client whose `get_parent_map` raises
`RunawayPaginationError`. Observed:

  WARNING fetcher: fetch_snapshot: parent enrichment failed
    (RunawayPaginationError('cursor stalled (probe)'));
    snapshot written without parent data (degraded)
  >>> SWALLOWED: fetch_snapshot RETURNED, snapshot written ... exists: True

The error did NOT propagate; a degraded snapshot was written and the pass reported success. That
outcome discriminates against the rival hypothesis that the transport-level re-raises at
acli_graph.py:304/394/477 are themselves incomplete: those re-raises fire correctly (the error
does escape the transport) — the loss is precisely one layer up, at the fetcher boundary, and it
is a type-hierarchy miss, not a missing handler.

DEFECT LEGITIMACY = defect. The intended behaviour is stated authoritatively in three places:
  * _backend.py:49-70 — "**Readers must re-raise this PAST their fail-open handlers.**" and it
    names "bug cabc (Cloud's `acli_graph` cursor walk)" as one of the three instances of the
    silent-loss class the type exists to guard.
  * acli_graph.py:29-38 — "Readers re-raise this PAST their fail-open handlers deliberately".
  * fetcher.py:511-516 — the `Raises:` contract already documents the stall error as
    "Deliberately re-raised PAST all three fail-open enrichment handlers".
Cloud's stall does not reach that contract. Additionally, bug cabc is a prior closed Fixed: ticket
for this exact behaviour class, which is itself authority that the behaviour is a defect.

CALLER-DEPENDENCY SWEEP (expected post-fix behaviour: a Cloud cursor stall aborts the pass instead
of degrading) — clear, no behavioural dependency blocks the fix:
  * `except RunawayPaginationError` at acli_graph.py:304/394/477 — unaffected, same class.
  * `except RuntimeError` sites — unaffected: `BackendPaginationStallError` itself subclasses
    `RuntimeError`, so `RuntimeError` stays in the MRO (the same reasoning already recorded at
    acli_subprocess.py:172).
  * the only other `except BackendPaginationStallError` outside fetcher is
    jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:96, which is DC-only and imports from `jira_datacenter/_base`,
    never `acli_graph` — it cannot see Cloud's error.
  * the three fetcher `except Exception` handlers ARE the dependency, and they are the defect.

FIX (as the ticket proposed, scope unchanged): `class RunawayPaginationError(BackendPaginationStallError)`.
adapters importing core is the established direction (jira_datacenter/_base.py:19 already does it).

rebar-debug FINAL REPORT — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1402.

PROBLEM. A stalled Cloud pagination cursor produced a silently degraded snapshot instead of
aborting the pass.

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE. `RunawayPaginationError` was declared `class RunawayPaginationError(RuntimeError)`
(acli_graph.py:29), so it sat outside `BackendPaginationStallError`'s hierarchy. `fetch_snapshot`'s
three enrichment re-raise clauses match on that CORE type (fetcher.py:621 parent, :668 comment,
:708 issuelink), so all three MISSED Cloud's error and the broad `except Exception` fail-open
beneath each (:625/:672/:712) swallowed it.

PROOF. Runtime, not static. Drove the real `fetch_snapshot` (loaded from source, `_load_acli`
patched) with a stub whose `get_parent_map` raises `RunawayPaginationError`:
  WARNING fetcher: parent enrichment failed (RunawayPaginationError(...)); snapshot written
  without parent data (degraded)  ->  SWALLOWED, snapshot written, pass returned.
This discriminates against the rival hypothesis that the transport re-raises (acli_graph.py:304/
394/477) are incomplete: those fire correctly — the loss is one layer up, and it is a type-hierarchy
miss, not a missing handler.

TEST (RED -> GREEN, held out). tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py,
+179 lines:
  * `test_a_cloud_cursor_stall_escapes_every_fetch_snapshot_enrichment_fail_open[parent|comment|
    issuelinks]` — a token-repeating Cloud REST stub driven through the REAL `fetch_snapshot`, with
    the REAL reader raising from the REAL shared `_iter_cursor_pages` walk (never an injected
    exception, which would prove only that `raise` re-raises). Keys on the requested `fields` so
    exactly one enrichment stalls per case and each handler is reached in turn.
  * `test_the_cloud_stall_error_is_the_core_stall_type` — the mechanism stated directly, plus
    `RuntimeError` must stay in the MRO.
  * `test_an_ordinary_enrichment_failure_still_fails_open_and_writes_the_snapshot[x3]` — negative
    control.
Verified RED first for the right reason (3x "DID NOT RAISE" with the swallow visible in the
captured log, plus the MRO assertion). The oracle was moved OUT of the tree before the fix subagent
ran, which was told the test path was off-limits and given only the root cause + contract. After
the fix: 49/49 green. MUTATION CHECK: restoring the `RuntimeError` base returned exactly those 4
tests to RED, then the fix was restored.

FIX. acli_graph.py, +13/-1: `class RunawayPaginationError(BackendPaginationStallError)`, the core
import, and a docstring paragraph recording why that base. fetcher.py untouched.

SCOPE & SAFETY.
  * Caller sweep clear: `except RunawayPaginationError` sites unaffected (same class);
    `except RuntimeError` sites unaffected (`BackendPaginationStallError` subclasses `RuntimeError`,
    so it stays in the MRO); jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:96 is DC-only and cannot see this error.
  * Restoration, not creation — no new entry point, command, or user-visible artifact.
  * No new dependency; the adapter->core import direction already exists (jira_datacenter/_base.py:19).
  * No test weakened: the 179 lines are purely additive, no pre-existing test body edited.
  * Regression: 2271 passed in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/; `make lint` and `make typecheck` green.

SIBLINGS (Step 7, both axes).
  * Construct sweep — the class is "an adapter-local pagination-stall error outside the core
    hierarchy". Only three types exist in this family repo-wide: `BackendPaginationStallError`
    (core), `RunawayPaginationError` (this fix), and `SilentTruncationError` (fetcher.py:108).
    One hit, fixed.
  * Parity census — rule: "a pagination stall raised by any adapter must be nameable by core's
    re-raise clauses." Cloud `adapters/jira` = was MISSING, fixed. DC `adapters/jira_datacenter`
    = holds (_base.py:187 raises the core type directly). `adapters/jira_family` = N/A, no pager.
    fetcher's own base-scan pager `_iter_pages` = N/A: its `SilentTruncationError` is raised from
    call sites at fetcher.py:397/:554, both ABOVE the enrichment try blocks, so no fail-open can
    absorb it (and fetcher.py:511 documents it as propagating). Dual-direction (outbound writes)
    = N/A, no whole-project paged read. No MISSING slot left undisposed.

RESIDUAL RISK. None observed beyond the fixed defect. The structural guard against recurrence is
the new `test_the_cloud_stall_error_is_the_core_stall_type` assertion: any future stall error that
drifts out of the core hierarchy fails it.

REPLICATION. The original report's scenario no longer reproduces — the same probe that printed
">>> SWALLOWED: snapshot written" now prints ">>> PROPAGATED".

# Cloud's `RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by `fetch_snapshot`'s three enrichment fail-opens

## Claim

Found in ticket 18a4's Phase-1 parity census (the fetcher-boundary axis).

DEFECT. Bug cabc's fix (ab7f, commit 30c522cde9) added `RunawayPaginationError` to Cloud's
`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:29` and made its three readers re-raise it past their OWN fail-open
handlers (`acli_graph.py:304, 394, 477`). That re-raise gets the error out of the transport — and
straight into `fetcher.fetch_snapshot`'s three broad `except Exception` enrichment handlers
(parent `fetcher.py:625`, comment `:672`, issuelink `:712`), which log a warning and degrade.

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; see the RCA comment)

`RunawayPaginationError` subclasses `RuntimeError`, NOT the core stall type. Live MRO:

    (RunawayPaginationError, RuntimeError, Exception, BaseException, object)
    issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError) == False

The three fetcher re-raise clauses match on the CORE type
(`except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` at `fetcher.py:621, 668, 708`), so they MISS Cloud's
error and control falls to the broad `except Exception` beneath each. Driving the real
`fetch_snapshot` with a stub whose `get_parent_map` raises `RunawayPaginationError` produced
`WARNING ... parent enrichment failed (RunawayPaginationError(...)); snapshot written without
parent data (degraded)` and a written snapshot — no propagation. A stalled Cloud cursor therefore
still yields a silently degraded snapshot that the differ treats as authoritative (missing parents
read as parentless; missing issuelinks read as "no links", so link removals become undetectable).

Intended behaviour is stated authoritatively at `_backend.py:49-70` ("Readers must re-raise this
PAST their fail-open handlers", naming bug cabc as an instance of the class), `acli_graph.py:29-38`,
and `fetcher.py:511-516`. cabc's fix is incomplete at the layer above the transport.

## Fix

Ticket 18a4 fixed exactly this hole on the DC side and built the mechanism this ticket needs:
`rebar_reconciler._backend.BackendPaginationStallError` (core, so `fetcher` can name it without
importing `adapters/`), plus `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` clauses already in place
ahead of all three fetcher enrichment handlers.

One-line change: make Cloud's error subclass the core one —
`class RunawayPaginationError(BackendPaginationStallError)` in `acli_graph.py`. The three fetcher
re-raise clauses then cover Cloud automatically. Keeping the Cloud-specific name preserves every
existing `except RunawayPaginationError` site and its tests unedited; `BackendPaginationStallError`
itself subclasses `RuntimeError`, so `except RuntimeError` sites are unaffected too. Adapters
importing core is the established direction (`jira_datacenter/_base.py:19` already does it).

NOT folded into 18a4 deliberately: this changes observable behaviour on the CLOUD surface (stalls
that previously degraded now abort the pass), which another work stream owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A stalled Cloud cursor propagates out of `fetch_snapshot` instead of degrading: a
      token-repeating Cloud stub driven through the REAL `fetch_snapshot` raises, for each of the
      three enrichment readers (`get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map`).
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`
- [x] `issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError)` is `True`, and
      `RuntimeError` remains in its MRO so existing `except RuntimeError` sites still catch it.
      Proof: asserted in the same test module.
- [x] Existing `except RunawayPaginationError` sites and their tests pass UNEDITED.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` with no edits to the pre-existing test bodies.
- [x] Ordinary (non-stall) enrichment failures still fail open and write a degraded snapshot
      (negative control: a plain `RuntimeError` from an enrichment reader must NOT propagate).
      Proof: negative-control case in the same test module.

## Testing

- RED-first held-out test added to
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`: a token-repeating Cloud
  REST stub driven through the real `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` (loaded from source, `_load_acli`
  patched), parameterized over all three enrichment readers, asserting the stall escapes. Verified
  failing before the fix and passing after; mutation-checked by restoring the `RuntimeError` base.
- Negative control in the same module: an ordinary `RuntimeError` enrichment fault still degrades
  and writes a snapshot carrying the base scan's issues.
- Regression: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

file_impact.reason: Re-base RunawayPaginationError on the core BackendPaginationStallError so fetcher.fetch_snapshot's three existing re-raise clauses cover Cloud; import the core type. One-line base-class change plus the import and a docstring note.

Held-out RED test: drive a token-repeating Cloud stub through the real fetch_snapshot and assert the stall escapes all three enrichment fail-opens; plus a negative control that an ordinary enrichment fault still degrades and writes a snapshot.
